summary.text: 家 is built from 宀, a roof or dwelling element, above a lower sign whose identity and role remain disputed. Early uses for human dwelling and household are reported; the evidence does not establish their order. Today it commonly means house, home, or family.

formation.text: The construction is disputed. One interpretation sees a pig beneath a roof, evoking livestock kept at home and possibly a pig enclosure; another follows the traditional analysis of 宀 plus an abbreviated 豭 used for sound. 家 and 豭 have matching readings in Mandarin and in the cited Middle and Old Chinese reconstructions, which makes the sound analysis plausible if 豭 is the relevant sign. The proposed pig-enclosure meaning and the identity of the earliest lower sign remain uncertain.

components.text: 宀 is the roof or dwelling element in the graph. It is a full component here; no separate earlier form is proposed.

The visible lower form is 豕. Some analyses read it as a pig contributing to a dwelling scene; the traditional analysis treats it as abbreviated 豭 used for sound. The sign’s earliest identity and role are unsettled. A proposal that it was originally 𢑓 and later altered to 豕 remains unverified.

sound_limitation.text: 家 and 豭 have compatible readings if 豭 is the relevant sign, but this does not establish that the visible 豕 represents 豭 or identify the earliest lower sign. No reading for proposed sign 𢑓 is established.

sound.text: 家 and 豭 share the modern Mandarin reading, supporting sound compatibility under the traditional analysis but not proving the lower sign’s identity.
The cited Middle Chinese readings match, supporting compatibility if 豭 is the relevant sign.
The cited Old Chinese reconstructions match, supporting compatibility if 豭 is the relevant sign.

history.text: In the regular-script form, 豕 appears beneath 宀. Shuowen describes the lower part as abbreviated 豭 used for sound; that analysis does not establish a graphic development from 豭 to 豕.
The proposal that an earlier lower sign 𢑓 was altered or misread as 豕 remains unverified, so the graphic sequence is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The lower element’s earliest identity and role are disputed: some analyses see a pig in a dwelling scene, while the traditional account treats it as an abbreviated sound element. “Pig enclosure” is a proposed original meaning, not an established one.
Matching readings for 家 and 豭 do not show that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No ancient pronunciation for the proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.text: Uses for human dwelling are reported in oracle-bone contexts. A pig-enclosure origin has been proposed, but is not established as the earliest meaning.

senses.gloss: ancestral temple, family, royal house or court, or counted household
senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their order and relationships are unclear.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these senses relate chronologically to the reported early uses is unresolved.

developments.text: Dwelling and household or institutional uses are both reported early, but their order and any development from one to the other are not established.
The modern senses are established, but their chronology and transition from the reported early uses are unresolved.

limitations.text: Reports of early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions, so the chronology of the senses remains unresolved.
The pig-enclosure account proposes a link from an enclosure to human dwelling; the traditional sound analysis offers a different account. Neither establishes the full history of the word’s meanings.
